title: The Live Asset Revisited
premise: Petra Dunmore, a ghost in the private security world, is approached by a stranger named Ilse Varga who claims he saved her life years ago in a training program he now runs — a debt Petra has no memory of incurring. As Varga's 'interest' escalates from surveillance to coercion, Petra realizes the program, Meridian, is grooming assets for a catastrophic operation timed to an upcoming Geneva summit. To survive and protect the makeshift family of misfits he's collected, Petra must infiltrate Meridian, expose its handlers, and burn the network that made him — even if it means finally admitting who he used to be. The story ends with the summit secured, Meridian dismantled, and Petra choosing, for the first time, to be seen.
about_author: Gideon Delacroix is the pen name of a former risk consultant who spent a decade advising firms on how to disappear. He writes thrillers about people whose professions require them to have no past.

chapters.title: The Favor That Never Happened
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. A quiet surveillance job ends when a stranger, Ilse Varga, buys Petra's coffee and calls it repayment for Lisbon, 2016 — an event Petra cannot recall. The beat is unease dressed as charm; Petra's instinct says the debt is real, just not his.

chapters.title: Household of Strays
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. We meet his found family: ex-analyst Mara, getaway driver Theo, and fixer June, who share a safehouse disguised as a renovation firm. Warmth against professionalism; Petra realizes how much he has to lose, which terrifies him more than any client.

chapters.title: Interest Accrued
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Varga's second contact is less gentle: photos of the safehouse, a file on each member of Petra's crew. He asks only for a small task — escort a courier. The beat is the trap closing slowly, politely.

chapters.title: The Courier
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The escort job goes sideways when the courier tries to kill Petra mid-route. Petra subdues him and finds a Meridian badge sewn into his lining. First confirmation the debt is recruitment; beat is cold dread.

chapters.title: Lisbon, 2016
chapters.summary: POV: Petra, intercut with fragmented memory. Digging through old contracts, Petra finds gaps in his own timeline — six missing weeks. Flashbacks surface: white rooms, obedience drills, a handler's voice. Beat: identity cracking open.

chapters.title: Mara Reads the File
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. She decrypts the dossier Varga left and discovers Meridian's structure: a private pipeline turning veterans and orphans into deniable operators. Her loyalty to Petra wars with what she learns he was. Beat: love tested by evidence.

chapters.title: The Handler's Voice
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. A phone call from a woman named Director Ashe — Varga's superior — offers Petra amnesty if he delivers three 'unreturned assets' before the Geneva summit. He refuses; she names his crew's real names. Beat: rage as clarity.

chapters.title: Theo's Run
chapters.summary: POV: Theo. Sent to shadow one of the unreturned assets, Theo botches the tail and gets made, forcing a violent escape through Marseille docks. His guilt and bravado crack; beat: the family's first real wound.

chapters.title: June's Bargain
chapters.summary: POV: June. She approaches an old intelligence contact to buy Meridian's org chart, paying with a favor she swore never to spend again. She succeeds but leaves a trail. Beat: sacrifice as quiet heroism.

chapters.title: The Org Chart
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. The chart reveals Meridian's endgame: a coordinated 'live asset' activation during the summit — simultaneous operations designed to look like state attacks. Beat: stakes crystallize from personal debt to public catastrophe.

chapters.title: Unreturned
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Petra tracks the first unreturned asset, Nadia, who ambushes him rather than be taken by anyone. Instead of fighting, he tells her the truth about her own missing weeks. Beat: two ghosts recognizing each other.

chapters.title: Nadia's Terms
chapters.summary: POV: Nadia. She agrees to help only if Petra burns Meridian entirely, not just dodges it. Together they plan infiltration via the program's alumni reunion — a vetting event before the summit. Beat: alliance forged from shared damage.

chapters.title: Reunion
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Inside the Meridian facility under a borrowed identity, Petra walks corridors his body remembers better than his mind. He passes vetting, but Varga watches him too closely. Beat: claustrophobic tension, the past wearing his face.

chapters.title: White Rooms
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Petra recovers enough memory to find the activation protocols and the list of summit-day targets. He copies them, nearly caught by Varga, and escapes through the facility's incinerator chute. Beat: terror transmuted into purpose.

chapters.title: Ashe's Countermove
chapters.summary: POV: Director Ashe. She anticipates the theft, leaks doctored files framing Petra's crew as Meridian operatives gone rogue, putting every police agency in Europe on them. Beat: the noose repositioned around innocent necks.

chapters.title: Fugitive Household
chapters.summary: POV: Mara. The crew scatters to a fallback safehouse, hunted. Mara counter-decrypts Ashe's frame job and finds the seam: a timestamp only the real thief could know. Beat: found family holding under maximum pressure.

chapters.title: The Second Asset
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Locating asset two, Dov, they find him already activated — a dead man walking through pre-summit rehearsals. Petra can't turn him off, only delay him, at cost of a gunshot wound. Beat: grief for what Meridian makes of people.

chapters.title: Interest Called Due
chapters.summary: POV: Varga. His POV reveals he engineered the 'favor' from the start — Petra was always the keystone asset, and the debt a leash. Yet Varga hesitates, remembering the man Petra might have been. Beat: antagonist humanized, not redeemed.

chapters.title: Geneva Eve
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Wounded and out of time, the crew converges on Geneva with proof, plans, and no official ally except a single skeptical summit security chief willing to listen. Beat: exhausted resolve before the storm.

chapters.title: Activation Day
chapters.summary: POV: rotating crew. As the summit opens, Meridian activates its remaining assets; the crew splits to intercept — Theo on the route, June on comms, Mara feeding the security chief live decryption. Beat: controlled chaos, everyone indispensable.

chapters.title: Burning the Network
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Petra confronts Ashe in the summit's service tunnels, exposes the operation to global feeds via Mara's uplink, and faces Varga one last time — letting him walk rather than become what Meridian built. Beat: climax as moral choice, not just violence.

chapters.title: Seen
chapters.summary: POV: Petra. Weeks later, Meridian is rubble, the crew legitimized as consultants, and Petra gives his real name — his first name, anyway — to the people who stayed. Beat: resolution as identity reclaimed; survival finally priced fairly.
